name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
description: An achievement-based scholarship awarding $20,000 to 150 high school seniors each year, judged on leadership, service, and academic excellence rather than financial need. Selection runs through multiple rounds, ending with a semifinalist interview weekend in Atlanta. One of the largest and most competitive corporate-funded scholarships in the United States.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, U.S. national, permanent resident, refugee, asylee, Cuban-Haitian entrant, or humanitarian parolee
eligibility.location: Must attend school in the 50 U.S. states, DC, Puerto Rico, or select Department of Defense schools
eligibility.excluded: Children and grandchildren of Coca-Cola system employees; international students; students who have already graduated high school

name: The Gates Scholarship
description: A last-dollar scholarship covering the full cost of attendance not already met by other financial aid, including tuition, fees, books, housing, food, and personal expenses. Successor to the Gates Millennium Scholars Program, it targets Pell-eligible high school seniors in roughly the top 10 percent of their class. No fixed dollar figure is published because the award scales to each recipient's unmet need.

eligibility.gpa_note: Minimum 3.3 cumulative weighted GPA on a 4.0 scale or equivalent
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or permanent resident
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time in a four-year degree program at an accredited, not-for-profit U.S. college or university

name: Cooke College Scholarship Program
description: A last-dollar undergraduate award worth as much as $55,000 per year for high-achieving high school seniors with financial need who plan to attend a top four-year college. The actual amount varies by tuition cost and other aid received. Recipients also get advising, a laptop, and access to internship and study-abroad funding.

eligibility.income_note: Family adjusted gross income up to $95,000
eligibility.enrollment: Intend to enroll at an accredited four-year college beginning fall 2027
eligibility.schooling: Must complete four years of high school in the U.S., a U.S. territory, or on a U.S. military base

requirements.test_scores: SAT, ACT, AP, or IB results required; no minimum score

name: Cooke Undergraduate Transfer Scholarship
description: A last-dollar award of as much as $55,000 per year for two to three years, for top community college students transferring to a four-year college or university to finish a bachelor's degree. Amounts vary by individual circumstances and other aid received. The application for the next cycle opens August 19, 2026; the closing date has not yet been published.

eligibility.enrollment: Current community college students seeking to complete a bachelor's degree at a four-year college or university

name: Elks Most Valuable Student Scholarship
description: Five hundred four-year scholarships awarded annually to graduating high school seniors, judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need. The top 20 recipients receive $30,000 total (up to $7,500 per year) and the remaining 480 receive $4,000 total. Applicants do not need any connection to an Elks member.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.enrollment: Four-year undergraduate degree program at an accredited U.S. college
eligibility.excluded: High school graduates are not eligible

name: Elks Legacy Award
description: A $6,000 scholarship paid as $1,500 per year for four years, awarded to 251 high school seniors who are children, grandchildren, step-children, step-grandchildren, or legal wards of a living Elks member. Awards are allocated by state and area, plus 149 at-large awards to the highest-scoring applicants nationwide.

eligibility.relationship: Child, grandchild, step-child, step-grandchild, or legal ward of a living Elk who joined on or before April 1, 2024
eligibility.sponsor_note: Sponsoring Elk must remain a dues-paying member through March 31, 2027

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
description: The oldest and most prestigious science and math competition for U.S. high school seniors, distributing about $3.1 million annually. The top 300 scholars each receive $2,000 (plus $2,000 for their school), 40 finalists travel to Washington DC, and the first-place winner receives $250,000. Entries must be original, independent research with completed data and results.

eligibility.citizenship: Any student in their last year of secondary school in the U.S. or its territories regardless of citizenship; U.S. citizens studying abroad also qualify
eligibility.project_type: Independent individual research only; collaborative projects, ideas without data, and literature reviews are not eligible

name: QuestBridge National College Match
description: Matches high-achieving, low-income high school seniors with full four-year scholarships to 55 partner colleges, a package the program values at over $360,000. Matched students are admitted early and graduate debt-free, with tuition, room, board, and fees covered and no loans in the package.

eligibility.income_note: Typically less than $65,000 annually for a household of four, with minimal assets
eligibility.academic_profile: Primarily A's in the most challenging courses available, strong writing, and intellectual curiosity

name: APIA Scholarship
provider_name: Asian & Pacific Islander American Scholars (APIA Scholars)
description: The largest scholarship program for Asian American and Pacific Islander students, offering one-year awards of $2,500 up to multi-year awards of $20,000. Priority goes to students with significant financial need, those living at or below the poverty line, and first-generation college students. The 2027-2028 application opens November 15, 2026.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, national, or legal permanent resident; citizens of the Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, and Palau also eligible
eligibility.enrollment: Enrolling or continuing as a degree-seeking undergraduate at an accredited U.S. college or university
eligibility.excluded: Students who already hold a bachelor's degree or higher
eligibility.priority: First-generation students and those at or below the poverty line

name: Dell Scholars Program
description: A $20,000 flexible scholarship for 500 students a year that covers tuition and housing and adds a laptop, textbook credits, and emergency funds, plus ongoing advising and career coaching. Notably it weights grit and determination over grades, requiring only a 2.4 GPA. Applications typically open in the fall and close in mid-February; the next cycle's exact deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.college_readiness_program: Must be participating in an approved college readiness program
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited four-year college or university immediately after high school

name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship Program
provider_name: The Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute
description: A $10,000 scholarship renewable for up to three additional years, worth up to $40,000 per recipient, awarded on demonstrated leadership, drive, integrity, and citizenship. The 2026 application has closed; the program typically opens in the fall with an early-January deadline, and students can sign up to be notified when the 2027 cycle opens.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited four-year U.S. college or university

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
description: Awards of $25,000, $50,000, and $100,000 to students 18 and under who have completed a significant piece of work in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, literature, music, philosophy, or an Outside the Box category. Judged on the work itself rather than grades or test scores. The 2027 application opens in fall 2026.

eligibility.age_note: Must be 18 or younger as of the application deadline
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, permanent resident residing in the U.S., or stationed overseas on active U.S. military duty

requirements.awards_ceremony_attendance: Must attend an in-person or virtual ceremony with at least one parent or guardian

name: Coolidge Scholarship
description: A full-ride presidential scholarship covering tuition, room, board, and required fees for four years of undergraduate study, plus an annual stipend for books and supplies, usable at any accredited U.S. college. Open to high school juniors and judged on academic excellence, interest in public policy, humility, and service. The foundation also names 100 Coolidge Senators from among top applicants. No fixed dollar value is published; the 2026-27 application opens in late summer or early fall 2026 with the deadline still to be announced.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident by the 2026-27 scholarship deadline
eligibility.enrollment: Must intend to enroll full-time as a first-time undergraduate at an accredited U.S. college or university in fall 2028
eligibility.excluded: Immediate family of employees, trustees, or donors giving more than $25,000 lifetime to the Coolidge Foundation

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
description: Covers unmet financial need up to $10,000 annually for up to three years, or until a bachelor's degree is earned, for students pursuing computer science and related fields. Deliberately low academic bar at a 2.3 GPA, with selection weighted toward substantial financial need. The 2025-2026 cycle is closed and the next opening has not been announced.

eligibility.citizenship: Must be authorized to work in the U.S. (citizen, permanent resident, or EAD holder)

name: HSF Scholar Program
description: Selects 10,000 HSF Scholars a year and awards over $30 million total, with individual awards from $500 to $5,000 based on relative need. Scholars also receive career services, mentoring, and leadership programming. Open to students of all races who identify as being of Hispanic heritage. The 2026 cycle closed February 15, 2026; the next cycle typically opens in December.

eligibility.heritage: Students of all races who identify as being of Hispanic heritage
eligibility.gpa_note: Minimum 3.0 for high school students; minimum 2.5 for college and graduate students
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, permanent legal resident, or DACA recipient
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited four-year university or graduate school

name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
description: Provides up to $35,000 over four years plus a comprehensive support program including a mentoring conference, career guidance, internship placement, and leadership development. Merit-based and open to all eligible students regardless of race or ethnicity. The most recent deadline was January 7, 2026; the next cycle's date has not been published.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.need_note: Must present evidence of financial need, evaluated case by case
eligibility.enrollment: Accredited, JRF-approved four-year U.S. college or university
eligibility.credits: Must not have completed more than 25 percent of college credits

name: Ron Brown Scholar Program
description: Awards $40,000 scholarships, paid as $10,000 a year for four years, to African American high school seniors who show academic excellence, leadership potential, and commitment to community service. The program is as much a lifelong network as a scholarship, with an active alumni community. Exact deadlines for the next cycle are not currently posted.

eligibility.criteria: Academic excellence, leadership potential, and commitment to community service

name: Posse Scholarship
description: A full-tuition leadership scholarship to one of Posse's partner colleges, awarded to students who are nominated by their high school or a community organization and selected through a group Dynamic Assessment Process. Scholars attend college in a supportive cohort of ten students from their city. Explicitly neither a minority nor a need-based scholarship. Nominations run spring through summer before senior year and deadlines vary by city, so no single dollar value or national date applies.

eligibility.nomination_note: Must be nominated by a registered high school or community-based organization in one of Posse's 20+ recruitment cities
eligibility.timing: Must be in the first term of senior year

name: Hagan Scholarship
description: One of the largest need-based awards available to students from small high schools, providing $2,000 for essential college startup items plus up to $7,500 each semester for up to eight consecutive semesters. Scholars also get funded study-abroad and internship support. Exact application open and close dates for the current cycle are not posted on the main page.

eligibility.income_note: Parents' adjusted household income must not exceed $125,000

name: Chick-fil-A Remarkable Futures Scholarship
description: Awards of $1,000, $2,500, and $25,000 to Chick-fil-A team members at franchised, company-owned, and affiliated restaurants, with $29 million distributed in 2026. Available to both full-time and part-time students and usable at any accredited school. Employment at a Chick-fil-A restaurant is required, so this is not open to the general public.

eligibility.employment_required: Must work at a franchised, company-owned, or affiliated Chick-fil-A restaurant
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time or part-time students both eligible

name: Folds of Honor Higher Education Scholarship
description: Need-based scholarships for spouses and dependents of fallen or disabled U.S. service members, and of first responders who have fallen or been catastrophically injured. Awards are based on unmet need with a cap of $2,500 per term ($1,250 part-time). The application window runs February 1 through March 31 each year, closing at 6:00 PM EST.

eligibility.relationship: Spouse or dependent of a fallen or disabled U.S. service member, or of a fallen or catastrophically injured first responder (firefighter, law enforcement, paramedic, EMT)
eligibility.gpa_note: Must maintain a 2.0 or higher term GPA for the two most recent academic terms
eligibility.schools: College, technical, trade, and post-graduate programs

name: Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation Scholarship
description: The nation's oldest and largest provider of need-based scholarships to military children, with awards ranging from $7,500 to $40,000 over four years. Children of the Fallen receive $30,000 over four years and Children of the Wounded up to $40,000. The undergraduate application window runs January 1 through March 1 annually; career and technical education applications are accepted year-round.

eligibility.relationship: Child of an active duty, reserve, or veteran U.S. Marine; a Marine killed in service; or Navy Corpsmen, Chaplains, and Religious Program Specialists attached to Marine units
eligibility.enrollment: Accredited, federally eligible school

name: Voice of Democracy Audio Essay Competition
description: A recorded audio essay competition for high school students, with a national first-place award of $35,000 paid directly to the winner's college, university, or vocational school. State winners receive a minimum of $1,000. The 2026-27 theme is "What a Veteran Taught Me About America" and entries are submitted through a local VFW Post.

requirements.format: Recorded audio essay submitted with a completed entry form to a local VFW Post
requirements.theme: What a Veteran Taught Me About America

name: Patriot's Pen Youth Essay Contest
description: A written essay contest for middle school students in grades 6 through 8, with a $5,000 national first-place award and state winners receiving a minimum of $500. Essays run 300 to 400 words on the annual patriotic theme, which for 2026-27 is "What a Veteran Taught Me About America." Entries go through a local VFW Post.

requirements.theme: What a Veteran Taught Me About America

name: Taco Bell Live Mas Scholarship
description: A passion-based scholarship judged on a short video rather than grades, test scores, or essays, with up to $14.5 million in total funding available and individual awards reported at $25,000 for top recipients. Open to anyone 16 to 26, whether or not they work at Taco Bell. The 2026 cycle ran October 14, 2025 to January 6, 2026 and is now closed.

eligibility.residency: Legal resident of the 50 U.S. states, DC, or a dependent child of active-duty military
eligibility.gpa_note: No GPA or test score requirement
eligibility.enrollment: On track to apply for, or currently enrolled in, an accredited post-secondary program

name: Ayn Rand Institute Essay Contests
description: Three annual essay contests based on the novels Anthem, The Fountainhead, and Atlas Shrugged, with prizes up to $25,000 and multiple awards available across the contests. Open worldwide to students age 13 and up, with Atlas Shrugged also open to college and graduate students. Deadlines for the current cycle are listed as to be determined.

eligibility.grade_note: Anthem and The Fountainhead are open to middle and high school students; Atlas Shrugged is open to high school, college, and graduate students
eligibility.enrollment: Must be enrolled in school during the contest period

name: Harry S. Truman Scholarship
description: The federal memorial to President Truman, providing up to $30,000 for graduate school to college juniors committed to careers in public service, plus priority graduate admission at partner programs, mentoring, and preferential federal hiring consideration. Candidates must be nominated by their institution rather than applying directly. The exact deadline for the next cycle is not posted.

eligibility.year_note: Penultimate year of school for students graduating in four years or more, or final year for students graduating in three years or fewer
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, U.S. national resident of American Samoa, or expecting citizenship by the award date
eligibility.public_service_commitment: Must plan to pursue graduate education leading to a public service career in government, uniformed services, public interest organizations, non-governmental research or educational organizations, public and private schools, or public-service nonprofits

name: Udall Undergraduate Scholarship
description: Up to 65 scholarships of $7,500 each for college sophomores and juniors who are future leaders in environmental fields, Tribal public policy, or Native American health care. Highly competitive and administered through a campus faculty representative. Exact deadline dates for the next cycle are published separately from the main program page.

name: Boren Scholarship
provider_name: Institute of International Education / National Security Education Program
description: Funds U.S. undergraduates to study critical languages in world regions underrepresented in study abroad, with awards of $8,000 for 8-11 weeks (STEM majors only), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, and $25,000 for the preferred 25-52 weeks. Languages include Arabic, Mandarin Chinese, Portuguese, Russian, and Swahili, and students of all proficiency levels are welcome. Comes with a one-year federal service requirement.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. undergraduate students
eligibility.language_study: Must study a critical language such as Arabic, Mandarin Chinese, Portuguese, Russian, or Swahili; all proficiency levels welcome
eligibility.service_requirement: One-year federal service requirement in a position supporting U.S. national security

name: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship
provider_name: U.S. Department of State / Institute of International Education
description: A federally funded award enabling Pell Grant recipients to study or intern abroad for academic credit, with an added supplement available for study of critical need languages. Recipients can receive the scholarship only once. The fall 2026 application opens in mid-August 2026 and closes October 1, 2026. The dollar amount is not stated on the program pages reviewed.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or national
eligibility.pell_note: Must be receiving a Federal Pell Grant at time of application, or prove they will receive one during the study abroad term
eligibility.enrollment: Undergraduate in good standing at an accredited U.S. institution, enrolled in or accepted to a credit-bearing study abroad or internship program
eligibility.destination: Program must be in a country with Travel Advisory Level 1 or 2

name: Burger King Scholars Program
description: Scholarships ranging from $1,000 to $60,000 for high school seniors as well as Burger King employees and their families, usable at college or post-secondary vocational and technical schools. The top tier is the James W. McLamore WHOPPER Scholarship Award of $60,000, granted to three students a year. Selection weighs GPA, work experience, extracurriculars, community service, and financial need; the program typically opens in mid-October and closes in December or once the application cap is reached.

eligibility.also_eligible: Burger King employees and their family members
eligibility.criteria: GPA, work experience, extracurricular activities, community service, and financial need

name: Milken Scholars Program
description: A $10,000 award paired with lifelong professional support, mentoring, graduate school counseling, and access to an alumni network, given to graduating seniors who combine academic achievement, community service, and resilience. Recruitment is limited to the Los Angeles, New York, and Washington DC areas, and candidates are nominated before applying. The class of 2026 application closed December 1, 2025; the next cycle's dates have not been posted.

name: NSBE National Scholarship Program
description: NSBE's national scholarship program funds members pursuing engineering, computer science, mathematics and related STEM degrees, with individual named awards including the Mamon & Cynthia Powers Scholarship at $10,000, the Analog Devices, Hatch, Angela Barbee and Tighe & Bond Scholarships at $5,000 each, and the NSBE Jr. Bridge Scholarship at $1,000. Applicants must be registered, paid NSBE members with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and must have their GPA verified by a school official through the MyNSBE portal. NSBE states that the Fall 2026 scholarship cycle will open soon; the Fall/Winter GPA verification window runs September 1, 2026 through February 26, 2027.

eligibility.other: Must be a registered, paid NSBE member. GPA must be self-reported on the MyNSBE profile and confirmed by a registered advisor or university official. Individual awards carry their own GPA minimums ranging from 2.0 to 3.0 and academic-level restrictions.

requirements.other: GPA verification by a school official through the MyNSBE portal is mandatory each semester. Applications are submitted through the NSBE Scholarships & Awards portal at nsbe.smapply.io.

name: IEEE PES Scholarship Plus Initiative
description: The IEEE PES Scholarship Plus Initiative supports undergraduate electrical and computer engineering students committed to careers in the power and energy field, paying $3,000 in the first year, $3,000 in the second and $4,000 in the third for up to $10,000 per qualifying scholar. Applicants must be full-time undergraduates at a U.S. ABET-accredited or Canadian CEAB-accredited university with a GPA of 3.0 or higher, and must complete or plan to complete three power-and-energy courses totaling nine credits. The application window opens January 20 annually with a deadline in mid-May; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: Citizen or permanent resident of the USA or Canada
eligibility.other: Must be a full-time undergraduate at a U.S. ABET-accredited or Canadian CEAB-accredited university. Must have completed or plan to complete 3 courses (9 credits) related to power and energy. IEEE PES Student Membership is not required for the first application but is required for renewal.

requirements.other: Online application through the IEEE PES scholarship portal.

name: Tau Beta Pi Scholarship
description: Tau Beta Pi awards approximately 250 scholarships each year to initiated members entering their senior year of undergraduate engineering study, worth $2,000 for a full year of enrollment or $1,000 for a single semester or partial year. Applicants must be initiated Tau Beta Pi members, or candidates who will be initiated by June 1, and must be full-time senior engineering undergraduates. The application deadline falls on April 1 each year with recommendation letters due April 8; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Must be an initiated Tau Beta Pi member, or a candidate for membership who will be initiated by June 1. Must be a full-time senior undergraduate engineering student. Students graduating in the fall semester may apply for partial scholarships.

requirements.other: Letters of recommendation are due one week after the application deadline.

name: ASCE Undergraduate Scholarships
description: ASCE offers nine named undergraduate scholarships for civil engineering students, including the Burton and Erma Lewis Structural Engineering Scholarship, the Lawrence W. and Francis W. Cox Scholarship, and the Eugene C. Figg, Jr. Civil Engineering Scholarship. ASCE states that its scholarships and fellowships generally offer $2,500 to $5,000 per recipient, though amounts vary year to year with the financial health of each endowment. Applications must be submitted online no later than January 15 of the year of award; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Undergraduate students with at least one year of study remaining. ASCE student membership is expected. Individual named scholarships carry their own additional criteria.

requirements.other: Online application through the ASCE awards portal.

name: AIAA Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
provider_name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Foundation
description: AIAA awards a slate of named undergraduate scholarships each year to AIAA Student Members pursuing science or engineering coursework leading into the aerospace field, ranging from $500 up to $10,000 for awards such as the Daedalus 88 Scholarship and the Mary W. Jackson Scholarship. Applicants must be current AIAA Student Members in good standing, enrolled at an accredited U.S. college, university or U.S. Territory institution, and must have completed at least one academic semester of full-time college work. The application opens at noon ET on October 15 each year and closes at 11:59 p.m. ET on January 31; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted with a year.

eligibility.citizenship: Must be enrolled at an accredited U.S. college or university or U.S. Territory institution
eligibility.other: Must be a current AIAA Student Member in good standing and have completed at least one academic semester of full-time college work. GPA exceptions: the Mary W. Jackson and Daedalus 88 Scholarships require a minimum 2.50.

requirements.other: 500 to 1,000 word essay on career objectives and academic program; college transcripts; two professional letters of recommendation submitted through the online system roughly two weeks after the application deadline; resume or CV.

name: AIAA Foundation Graduate Award
provider_name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Foundation
description: AIAA's graduate awards fund master's and doctoral students conducting aerospace-related research, with the Neil Armstrong Graduate Award and the Orville and Wilbur Wright Graduate Award at $10,000 each and two Dr. Hassan A. Hassan Graduate Awards in Aerospace Engineering at $9,000 each. Applicants must be current AIAA Student Members who have completed at least one academic quarter or semester of full-time graduate work. The application opens October 15 and closes January 31 each year; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted with a year.

eligibility.citizenship: Varies by award: the Neil Armstrong Graduate Award requires U.S. citizenship, while the Orville and Wilbur Wright Graduate Award allows enrollment worldwide
eligibility.other: Must be a current AIAA Student Member in good standing and have completed at least one academic quarter or semester of full-time graduate-level work. The Neil Armstrong Award requires a 3.0 GPA minimum.

requirements.other: 500 to 1,000 word career-objectives essay; transcripts including all graduate work through the most recent fall term; two professional letters of recommendation; resume or CV; plus a one to three page double-spaced research description defining hypotheses, approach, objectives and benefits.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
description: Amazon Future Engineer awards renewable scholarships to U.S. high school seniors planning to pursue a bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, covering unmet financial need up to a maximum of $10,000 annually for up to four years. Recipients also receive a paid summer internship at Amazon. Applications for the most recent cycle have closed and Amazon has not yet announced the next cycle's dates; the program has historically opened in the fall with a winter deadline.

eligibility.citizenship: Must be authorized to work in the United States
eligibility.other: Must be a U.S. high school senior who has taken computer science coursework or passed Amazon's assessment, must demonstrate financial need, and must plan to pursue a bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field.

requirements.other: Demonstration of financial need is required. Applications are submitted through Scholarship America.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search 2027
description: The Regeneron Science Talent Search is the nation's oldest and most prestigious science and mathematics competition for high school seniors, distributing $3.1 million in awards annually. Each of the top 300 scholars receives $2,000 with a matching $2,000 to their high school, the top 40 finalists receive an all-expenses-paid trip to Washington, DC, and the grand prize is $250,000. Entrants must submit an original, independent research project with completed data and results, along with a maximum 20-page scientific paper, essays, recommendations and transcripts.

eligibility.citizenship: Any student may enter regardless of citizenship, provided they are living in and attending their last year of secondary school in the US or its territories
eligibility.other: Must be in the last year of secondary school in the US or its territories. Research conducted during any year of high school is eligible. Entries must be original, independent, individual research with completed data and results, not project ideas or literature reviews.

requirements.other: A maximum 20-page original scientific research paper, essay questions, questions about the student and project, recommendations, transcripts and optional test scores. All materials including recommendations must be submitted by 8:00 p.m. ET on the deadline.

name: Barry Goldwater Scholarship
provider_name: Barry Goldwater Scholarship and Excellence in Education Foundation
description: The Goldwater Scholarship is the premier undergraduate award in the United States for students intending research careers in the natural sciences, mathematics and engineering, worth up to $7,500 per academic year toward tuition, fees, books, and room and board. Students cannot apply directly; each participating institution may nominate up to four students annually, plus one additional nominee who is a transfer student or veteran. The Foundation's nomination deadline falls on the last Friday in January at 5:00 p.m. CT, and individual campus deadlines are substantially earlier and vary by institution.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or U.S. national
eligibility.other: Must be a college sophomore or junior with strong academic performance and research experience, intending a research career. Must be nominated by a participating institution through its campus representative; students may not apply directly.

requirements.other: A research essay is required. Students work with their campus representative to prepare materials and submit through the online portal; the campus representative then formally nominates.

name: Astronaut Scholarship
description: The Astronaut Scholarship Foundation awards scholarships of up to $15,000 to exceptional STEM juniors and seniors who intend to conduct research or otherwise advance their field, along with a paid trip to the Innovators Symposium and Gala and lifetime engagement with the Foundation. Students cannot apply directly; faculty at ASF-affiliated universities must nominate candidates they know well enough to identify a special drive or talent foreshadowing a creative career. The nomination deadline for the most recent cycle was March 30, 2026 and the next cycle's date has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, native-born or naturalized
eligibility.other: Must be a sophomore applying for junior year or a junior applying for senior year, enrolled full-time for both semesters at a participating ASF university. Biomedical researchers are eligible; pre-med and clinical medicine students are not. Requires faculty nomination through a campus liaison.

requirements.other: Two recommendation letters, a one-page personal statement, academic transcripts, and a CV or resume, submitted after faculty nomination.

name: Hertz Fellowship
description: The Hertz Fellowship is one of the most competitive graduate awards in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics and engineering, providing up to five years of funding valued at up to $250,000 plus lifelong access to the Hertz community. The fellowship supports doctoral students and is designed to give recipients freedom from the constraints of traditional research funding. Application dates are published on the Foundation's application pages and the current cycle's dated deadline is not posted on the main fellowship page; the program has historically opened in the summer with an autumn deadline.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and DACA recipients
eligibility.other: For students pursuing a PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics and engineering. College seniors, first-year graduate students and those in the early stages of doctoral study are the target applicant pool.

requirements.other: Written application followed by two rounds of technical interviews.

name: SMART Scholarship-for-Service Program
description: The Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship-for-Service Program pays full tuition at any regionally accredited U.S. college or university plus annual stipends ranging from $30,000 to $46,000, along with summer internships at DoD facilities and guaranteed civilian employment after graduation. Recipients accept a one-for-one post-graduation service commitment as a civilian DoD employee, serving one year for each year of funding. The application period opens annually on August 1 and closes the first Friday in December.

eligibility.citizenship: Citizen of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or the United Kingdom
eligibility.other: Must be pursuing a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree in a supported STEM discipline and maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. High school seniors and incoming freshmen are eligible. Must accept a one-for-one service commitment as a civilian DoD employee.

requirements.other: Full tuition plus stipend, book allowance, health insurance allowance and paid summer internships are included in the award.

name: CyberCorps: Scholarship for Service (SFS)
provider_name: U.S. National Science Foundation and U.S. Office of Personnel Management
description: CyberCorps: Scholarship for Service provides up to three years of support for cybersecurity undergraduate and graduate education at participating institutions, with annual stipends of $27,000 for undergraduates and $37,000 for graduate students plus tuition and required fees. Recipients must serve in a qualified government organization for a period at least equal to the length of the scholarship. Students apply through their own participating institution rather than centrally, so deadlines vary by school and most institutional windows fall between April and June.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident
eligibility.other: Must be a full-time student in a coherent formal program at a participating institution, at sophomore standing for an associate's degree, junior or senior standing for a bachelor's, master's enrollment, or research-based doctoral enrollment. Must demonstrate a commitment to a career in AI or cybersecurity.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted to the SFS program at the student's own participating institution; each institution sets its own required materials and deadline.

name: ISACA Foundation Scholarship Program
description: The ISACA Foundation runs a global scholarship program for students pursuing degrees related to IT audit, risk, cybersecurity, governance and assurance, with awards ranging from $500 to $7,500. A single application is matched against a large slate of named and chapter-specific scholarships including the Digital Trust Scholarship, the SheLeadsTech Scholarship and the National Cyber League Games Scholarship. The program runs two cycles per year; Cycle 2 for 2026 opens September 8 and closes October 20.

eligibility.citizenship: Not restricted; several scholarships are open worldwide while others are limited to specific U.S. metro areas or countries
eligibility.other: Individual scholarships within the program carry their own school-specific or region-specific eligibility, including awards restricted to Greater Philadelphia, Greater St. Louis, Puerto Rico and Madison, Wisconsin.

requirements.other: Single online application through the ISACA Foundation scholarship platform; applicants are automatically matched to all scholarships they qualify for.

name: Samantha Jennings-Jones Memorial Scholarship
provider_name: Center for Cyber Safety and Education (ISC2)
description: This $5,000 award is given annually to support a woman seeking to start or advance a career in cybersecurity, granted through the Center for Cyber Safety and Education's academic scholarship program. Recipients may also take the ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity certification exam at no cost. The 2026 cycle closed March 15, 2026; the Center historically opens academic scholarship applications in the winter with a mid-March deadline, and the next cycle has not been announced.

eligibility.citizenship: Applicants from any country
eligibility.other: Open to students pursuing or planning to pursue a cybersecurity-focused degree, enrolled full-time or part-time, at on-campus or online programs. This award specifically supports a woman in cybersecurity.

requirements.other: Applied for through the Center's academic scholarship application at iamcybersafe.org.

name: AFCEA Cyber Security Scholarship
description: A $5,000 scholarship for full-time undergraduates enrolled in cybersecurity, computer science, digital forensics, information assurance or related cyber fields at a four-year accredited U.S. institution. It is awarded from AFCEA's single STEM Majors application, which also considers applicants for the STEM Major Scholarship and the Student Member Scholarship. The 2026 cycle has closed with supporting documents having been due May 1, 2026; AFCEA typically opens the STEM Majors application in the winter and the next cycle has not been announced.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or permanent resident
eligibility.other: Must be enrolled full-time at a four-year accredited U.S. college or university and be a sophomore or junior at the time of application.

requirements.other: At least one letter of recommendation from a professor at the applicant's current institution, submitted by the recommender as a PDF to edfoundation@afcea.org; official transcripts covering all college-level coursework submitted electronically by the school. An additional recommendation letter or resume is optional.

name: AFCEA STEM Major Scholarship
description: A $2,500 scholarship for full-time undergraduate sophomores and juniors majoring in STEM fields relevant to national security communications and information technology, spanning more than 26 qualifying technical programs including computer science, electrical engineering, mathematics, physics and aerospace engineering. Awards may be applied only toward tuition and required course-related expenses including fees, books, supplies and equipment. The 2026 cycle has closed and the next cycle has not been announced; AFCEA typically opens the STEM Majors application in the winter.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or permanent resident
eligibility.other: Must be enrolled full-time at a four-year accredited U.S. college or university and be a sophomore or junior at the time of application.

requirements.other: At least one letter of recommendation from a professor at the applicant's current institution; official transcripts covering all college-level coursework submitted electronically by the school.

name: Nightwing Scholarship
description: A $5,000 scholarship applied toward tuition for students pursuing cyber intelligence and cybersecurity-related degrees at an accredited community college or four-year college or university. Eligible majors include cybersecurity, computer science, cybersecurity engineering, information security and assurance, cyber intelligence and security, cybersecurity risk management, intelligence analysis and artificial intelligence. The 2026 cycle has closed and the next cycle has not been announced.

eligibility.other: Undergraduates must be in their sophomore, junior or senior year, or pursuing a master's degree. Must demonstrate strong academic performance and aptitude for STEM subjects and be in good standing with a minimum 3.0 unweighted GPA.

requirements.other: A brief essay of 250 words or less describing financial need; at least one letter of recommendation from a professor at the applicant's current institution; official transcripts covering all college-level coursework.

name: Howard A. Schmidt Memorial Scholarship
description: A $3,500 scholarship for undergraduate students pursuing a career in cybersecurity, awarded by the Information Systems Security Association Education Foundation. Applicants must be enrolled full-time as a sophomore or above and must show security-related work experience or completed security coursework. The ISSAEF scholarship application period runs February 1 to June 15 each year; the 2026 window closed June 15, 2026 and the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Enrolled full-time as a sophomore or above; must have security-related work experience and/or completed security coursework; must be pursuing a cybersecurity career.

requirements.other: Personal statement describing background and goals; unofficial transcript; at least one letter of recommendation, with two preferred.

name: E. Eugene Schultz, Jr. Memorial Scholarship
description: A $3,500 scholarship for graduate students pursuing a career in cybersecurity, awarded by the Information Systems Security Association Education Foundation. Graduate applicants must hold a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher and must show security-related work experience or completed security coursework. The ISSAEF scholarship application period runs February 1 to June 15 each year; the 2026 window closed June 15, 2026 and the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Enrolled full-time in graduate studies; must have security-related work experience and/or completed security coursework; must be pursuing a cybersecurity career.

requirements.other: Personal statement describing background and goals; unofficial transcript; at least one letter of recommendation, with two preferred.

name: Shon Harris Women in Security Memorial Scholarship
description: A $2,000 scholarship for women pursuing either undergraduate or graduate studies toward a cybersecurity career, awarded by the Information Systems Security Association Education Foundation. Applicants must show security-related work experience or completed security coursework, with undergraduates needing a 2.5 GPA and graduate students a 3.0. The ISSAEF scholarship application period runs February 1 to June 15 each year; the 2026 window closed June 15, 2026 and the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Open to women in security. Enrolled full-time as a sophomore or above for undergraduates, or in graduate studies. Graduate applicants require a 3.0 GPA; undergraduates require 2.5.

requirements.other: Personal statement describing background and goals; unofficial transcript; at least one letter of recommendation, with two preferred.

name: AOPA Foundation Aviation Scholarship Program
provider_name: AOPA Foundation (Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association)
description: The AOPA Foundation funds flight training toward primary pilot certificates, advanced ratings and aviation maintenance careers, with numerous awards ranging from $250 to $14,000. A single general application automatically matches applicants to every scholarship they qualify for, and funds are disbursed directly to recipients on a prepaid expense card. The Fall 2026 application period runs October 1 through December 31, 2026, with all applicants receiving a decision email by April 15, 2027.

eligibility.citizenship: Open to residents of the United States and District of Columbia, Canada, Guam, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands
eligibility.other: Must be a current AOPA member; complimentary high school membership is available. Applicants need not be enrolled in an aviation program or pursuing an aviation career. You may apply having already started flight training but become ineligible if you pass your checkride before the award. The high school track is for ages 16 to 18.

requirements.other: Completed online application with written responses; a recent transcript including current school year grades and cumulative unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale; two references submitted on AOPA's provided reference form, where parents, other relatives and same-age friends are disqualifying. Flight training must be completed within 12 months of the award date.

name: Vertical Flight Foundation Scholarship
description: The Vertical Flight Foundation awards scholarships ranging from $4,000 to $6,000 to engineering students whose studies relate to vertical flight technology, presented at an annual awards ceremony each May. The top-ranked applicant receives the $6,000 Bell scholarship, and the applicant showing the most interest in improving vertical flight affordability is considered for the Jing Yen Cost Awareness scholarship. A student may receive a VFF scholarship only once per academic level, meaning once as an undergraduate, once as a master's student and once as a doctoral student.

eligibility.other: Must be enrolled full-time in a relevant engineering degree program at an accredited university and have at least one academic term remaining after the May award ceremony. High school students are ineligible. The application deadline has historically fallen on February 1 and the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

requirements.other: Completed application form; a personal narrative demonstrating passion for vertical flight technology; resume; official transcript sent directly by the registrar's office; and a letter of recommendation from a professor. Cost Awareness applicants must explicitly address affordability in vertical flight.

name: Choose Aerospace Scholarship
provider_name: Choose Aerospace (with the Aviation Technician Education Council)
description: Choose Aerospace awards $2,500 cash scholarships to students entering or enrolled in aviation maintenance technical programs, funded by industry donors. Beyond the cash award the program distributes in-kind awards including Sonic Tools aviation tool kits valued at $7,102, Avotek textbook sets and General Familiarization Courses. The next application cycle opens November 1, 2026; the official page announces the opening date but does not publish a closing date.

eligibility.other: Must be planning to attend or be currently enrolled at an aviation technical program. Priority consideration may be given to students attending ATEC member institutions.

requirements.other: Application is hosted on chooseaerospace.org; detailed document requirements are published when the application opens.

name: Alice T. Schafer Mathematics Prize
description: The Alice T. Schafer Prize recognizes women undergraduates who have demonstrated excellence in mathematics, with winners each receiving a $1,000 prize and an honorary certificate. The nomination period runs August 1 through September 15 each year. Anyone may nominate, self-nominations are permitted, and AWM membership is not required.

eligibility.other: The nominee must be an undergraduate at the time of nomination. Nominations of women from underrepresented minorities are especially encouraged.

requirements.other: Submission is a single compiled PDF via MathPrograms.org containing a nomination letter of at most three pages, student transcripts showing expected graduation date, an optional supporting-materials section, and a contact-information cover sheet. Self-nominators must provide one additional letter of support.

name: CAS Trust Scholarship
description: The CAS Trust Scholarship is a merit-based award for full-time college students pursuing a career in property and casualty actuarial science, awarding scholarships of $5,000 and $2,500. Applicants must have already sat for at least one actuarial exam and be members of CAS Student Central, which is free to join. The program historically opens in the fall with a January 31 deadline; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Must be currently attending college or university as a full-time student and continuing as a full-time student in the following academic year; must have sat for at least one actuarial exam; must be a member of CAS Student Central.

requirements.other: Online application with an attached essay; two recommendation letters, preferably from individuals with a direct relationship who can speak to your potential as a future actuary; a current transcript plus prior transcripts if needed. It is the student's responsibility to ensure recommendation letters are submitted by the deadline.

name: STEM Stars Actuarial Scholars Program
description: STEM Stars is a four-year renewable scholarship for high school students skilled in math who are interested in the actuarial field, providing $5,000 annually for up to four years for a total of $20,000. Recipients also receive mentorship, networking and internship experiences designed to prepare them for an actuarial career. The 2026 application season is closed and The Actuarial Foundation states the application will reopen in fall 2026.

eligibility.other: Open to high school students who are skilled in math and interested in the actuarial field.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted through The Actuarial Foundation's Submittable portal. Detailed document requirements are published when the application opens.

name: Actuary of Tomorrow - Stuart A. Robertson Memorial Scholarship
provider_name: The Actuarial Foundation (administered by Scholarship America)
description: The Robertson Memorial Scholarship supports undergraduates who have already demonstrated commitment to the actuarial profession by passing at least two actuarial exams, with awards ranging from $2,500 to $10,000. Applicants must have at least sophomore standing and maintain a 3.0 GPA. The program runs on a spring cycle and the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: Must plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university in the United States
eligibility.other: Must be a current college undergraduate with a minimum sophomore standing and must have successfully completed at least two actuarial exams.

requirements.other: Current complete transcript showing student name, school name, grades and credit hours; copies of results from a minimum of two actuarial exams taken and passed; two letters of reference, one from a current or previous employer and one from a professor or advisor.

name: OLA Cresta Scholarship
description: The Organization of Latino Actuaries awards scholarships to students attending U.S. colleges and universities who are interested in the actuarial profession, with the top-ranked student receiving the $7,500 OLA Cresta Scholarship. Applications open January 1 and close March 31 each year. No letters of recommendation are required.

eligibility.citizenship: Must be attending a U.S. college or university in the upcoming school year
eligibility.other: Open to students who will be attending a U.S. college or university in the next school year and are interested in the actuarial profession. High school seniors enrolled in a U.S. college or university program for the upcoming academic year are eligible.

requirements.other: OLA's FAQ states that letters of recommendation are not required. Additional document requirements are published in the application.

name: AANP Student Scholarship
description: AANP awards scholarships of $2,500 to $5,000 to student members enrolled in accredited graduate nurse practitioner programs, with payments made directly to the institution and designated for tuition only. In the 2026 cycle AANP awarded a total of $155,000 across four grants and 27 scholarships. The 2026 cycle closed March 18, 2026; AANP typically opens the application in the winter and the next cycle has not been announced.

eligibility.other: Must be a licensed registered nurse enrolled in an accredited graduate school and program, have at least one semester of the current program completed, and complete the program with a master's or doctoral degree in nursing or a related field. AANP membership is required. Board members, their relatives, and previous scholarship recipients are ineligible.

requirements.other: NP program of study, official transcripts, accreditation verification, two professional references on letterhead, and a current CV or resume.

name: Alpha Mu Tau Clinical Laboratory Science Scholarships
provider_name: Alpha Mu Tau Fraternity and the ASCLS Education and Research Fund
description: A slate of named undergraduate and graduate scholarships worth $2,000 to $3,000 for students in NAACLS-accredited medical laboratory science and medical laboratory technician programs, plus approved master's and doctoral programs. One application covers all undergraduate awards and a separate application covers all graduate awards. The published deadline is March 1 each year, extended to April 1 in 2026; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen or permanent U.S. resident
eligibility.other: Must be attending a U.S. institution of higher learning, be a member of ASCLS, and be accepted into a NAACLS-accredited MLS or MLT program. Undergraduate applicants must be in or entering the last year of their program and cannot complete their education before September 30. Graduate applicants cannot complete their education before September 1.

requirements.other: Two letters of recommendation and two performance score sheets, one set from the NAACLS Program Director and one from a non-relative professional or personal reference, submitted directly by evaluators. Official transcripts from each college must be sent directly by the institution. Only type-written applications are evaluated.

name: AAUW Selected Professions Fellowships
description: AAUW Selected Professions Fellowships carry a stipend of $20,000 for women pursuing full-time master's study in science, technology, engineering or mathematics, or professional degrees in medicine, dentistry, optometry, chiropractic or podiatry. The fellowships target fields in which women have historically been underrepresented. The 2027 application window opens January 5, 2027 and closes February 18, 2027 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizens, nationals, or permanent residents from the 50 states, D.C., Puerto Rico, Guam, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, or any other territory
eligibility.other: Applicants must identify as a woman and must be pursuing full-time master's study in a designated STEM field or a professional degree in a designated health profession.

requirements.other: Two letters of recommendation; copies of all degrees earned to date; official transcripts confirming conferral of all degrees received; proof of admission or current enrollment documentation if applicable.

name: AAUW Career Development Grants
description: AAUW Career Development Grants support women who hold at least an associate's degree and are pursuing coursework, professional development or credentials in fields where women are underrepresented, explicitly including STEM, engineering, technology, architecture, mathematics and the natural sciences. The award ceiling is $8,000 and actual award sizes vary. Two windows run each year: the Winter/Spring 2027 window opens August 18, 2026 and closes September 30, 2026, and the Summer/Fall 2027 window runs January 27 to March 18, 2027.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizens, nationals, or permanent residents from the 50 states, D.C., Puerto Rico, Guam, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, or any other territory
eligibility.other: Applicants must identify as a woman and must hold at least an associate's degree or higher. The proposed field must be one in which women comprise less than 50 percent of the workforce or senior leadership.

requirements.other: Proof of highest degree by diploma copy or official transcript with conferral date; official transcript confirming degree conferral; documented proof that women are underrepresented in the proposed field, using current data from reputable sources.

name: A.T. Anderson Memorial Scholarship
provider_name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: AISES' flagship scholarship supports Indigenous students pursuing a degree in any STEM field, awarding $1,000 to undergraduates and $2,000 to graduate students. Applicants must be current AISES members, which is free for students, and full-time students carrying 12 or more credit hours at an accredited college or university. The AISES scholarship cycle opens December 15 and closes April 30 each year; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Must be an enrolled citizen or descendant of an enrolled citizen of a federal or state recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Village, or Native Hawaiian or descendant, or Pacific Islander or descendant, or an Indigenous person of Canada. Must be a current AISES member and a full-time student carrying 12 or more credit hours.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted through the AISES OASIS portal. Tribal enrollment documentation or a CDIB card may be required.

name: AISES ARDC Scholarship
provider_name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: A $5,000 scholarship funded by Amateur Radio Digital Communications for Indigenous students in electrical engineering, computer engineering, web design and development, audio technology, mechanical engineering, mathematics, information technology, communications or related fields. Applicants must be current AISES members and full-time students. The AISES scholarship cycle opens December 15 and closes April 30 each year; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Must be an enrolled citizen or descendant of an enrolled citizen of a federal or state recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Village, or Native Hawaiian or descendant, or Pacific Islander or descendant, or an Indigenous person of Canada. Must be a current AISES member and a full-time student carrying 12 or more credit hours.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted through the AISES OASIS portal. Tribal enrollment documentation or a CDIB card may be required.

name: Polaris Academic Scholarship
provider_name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: A $5,000 scholarship funded by Polaris for Indigenous students in mechanical engineering, digital and information technology, manufacturing and supply chain, or other STEM-related fields. Applicants must be current AISES members and full-time students at an accredited college or university. The AISES scholarship cycle opens December 15 and closes April 30 each year; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Must be an enrolled citizen or descendant of an enrolled citizen of a federal or state recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Village, or Native Hawaiian or descendant, or Pacific Islander or descendant, or an Indigenous person of Canada. Must be a current AISES member and a full-time student carrying 12 or more credit hours.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted through the AISES OASIS portal. Tribal enrollment documentation or a CDIB card may be required.

name: AISES Stellantis MCAP Scholarship
provider_name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: A Stellantis-funded scholarship awarding $6,500 per year for up to two years plus a $7,000 tool allotment, supporting Indigenous students in automotive technology and related technical fields. Applicants must be current AISES members and must complete tribal citizenship verification. The AISES scholarship cycle opens December 15 each year with a May 30 deadline for this award; the next cycle's dated deadline has not been posted.

eligibility.other: Must be an enrolled citizen or descendant of an enrolled citizen of a federal or state recognized American Indian Tribe or Alaska Native Village, or Native Hawaiian, Pacific Islander, or Indigenous person of Canada. Must be a current AISES member. Tribal citizenship verification is required.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted through the AISES OASIS portal. Includes a $7,000 tool allotment in addition to the cash award.

name: HSF Scholarship
description: The Hispanic Scholarship Fund's flagship need-based award is open to students of all races who identify as being of Hispanic heritage, at the high school, undergraduate and graduate levels, with amounts ranging from $500 to $5,000 based on relative need. All majors qualify although HSF places particular emphasis on STEM fields. The 2026-2027 cycle ran January 5 to February 15, 2026; HSF opens its application in early January each year and the next cycle has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen, permanent legal resident, or DACA recipient
eligibility.other: Must identify as being of Hispanic heritage. Minimum 3.0 GPA for high school applicants and minimum 2.5 GPA for college and graduate students. Must plan to enroll full-time at an accredited public or not-for-profit four-year university or graduate school in the U.S.

requirements.other: Must complete and submit the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) for the corresponding academic year.

name: NACME Block Scholarship
provider_name: National Action Council for Minorities in Engineering
description: NACME provides $5,000 scholarships to high-achieving college students pursuing careers in engineering and computer science, awarded through partner institutions including Texas A&M University, UC San Diego, the University of Delaware and the University of Georgia, plus corporate scholar programs with Bechtel, Boston Scientific, GE Healthcare, GE Vernova and GlobalFoundries. Students submit a single common application for consideration across current and future awards. Deadlines vary by award from September 1 through December 31, 2026, with three of the four block scholarships closing September 11, 2026.

eligibility.other: Bachelor's degree candidates with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Block scholarships are tied to specific partner universities; corporate scholar awards may include a paid internship component.

requirements.other: Submit the NACME common application for initial consideration across current and future awards.

name: L'Oreal USA For Women in Science Fellowship
provider_name: L'Oreal USA (administered by the American Association for the Advancement of Science)
description: Five postdoctoral research grants of $75,000 each are awarded annually to women scientists in STEM fields, administered by AAAS on behalf of L'Oreal USA. Applicants must hold a PhD, DPH or ScD and be a current or incoming postdoctoral associate affiliated with a U.S.-based academic institution. The 2026 application closed February 13, 2026; the application typically opens in the fall and the next cycle has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: American citizens, born or naturalized, or permanent residents holding a green card. J1, H1-B and F1 visa holders are not eligible.
eligibility.other: Must identify as a woman and hold a PhD, DPH or ScD conferred on or before the cycle cutoff; candidates exclusively holding other degrees including MD and DVM are not eligible. Must be a current postdoctoral associate or begin the position by the cycle cutoff, affiliated with a U.S.-based academic institution. Awardees must be available for the For Women in Science Awards Week, typically held in November.

requirements.other: Application submitted through the AAAS secure platform, including a research proposal and a budget prepared on the provided template.

name: SASE Parker Hannifin Scholarship
provider_name: Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers
description: A $5,000 scholarship sponsored by Parker Hannifin for SASE Collegiate and Professional members demonstrating excellence in STEM, evaluated on academic achievement, leadership credentials and community contributions. The 2026 cycle opened April 16 and closed May 22, 2026, with disbursements beginning July 27, 2026. The next cycle has not yet been announced; SASE typically opens its scholarship applications in the spring.

eligibility.other: Must be a SASE Collegiate or Professional member. Evaluated on exceptional academic achievements, leadership credentials and community contributions. Specific GPA minimums are not published.

requirements.other: Applications are submitted through an external portal linked from the SASE scholarship page; questions go to scholarship@saseconnect.org.

name: Texas Interscholastic League Foundation (TILF) Scholarship
description: Awards for Texas high school seniors who competed at a UIL Academic State Meet, Congressional Debate State Meet, One-Act Play State Meet, or Theatrical Design State Meet. Participation only in athletic or music contests does not qualify. Recipients must attend an accredited Texas college or university, enroll full-time, and maintain a 2.5 college GPA. The application window historically opens in the spring and closed May 22 for the prior cycle; the next cycle's date has not been posted.

eligibility.residency: Graduating from a Texas high school during the current academic year
eligibility.college_location: Accredited college or university in Texas
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time
eligibility.activity_requirement: Competed at a UIL Academic, Congressional Debate, One-Act Play, or Theatrical Design State Meet

requirements.test_scores: SAT or ACT scores on transcript
requirements.tax_documents: Pages 1 and 2 of parent/guardian most recent IRS Form 1040

name: Texas PTA High School Senior Scholarship
description: A $1,000 scholarship for graduating Texas high school seniors who are current PTA/PTSA members at a campus with a Local PTA/PTSA in Active Status. The application opens September 15 and closes November 15; PTA membership must be in place by December 1. Recipients are announced by April 1.

eligibility.residency: Enrolled in a Texas high school
eligibility.membership: Current PTA/PTSA member at enrolled campus by December 1; campus PTA must reach Active Status by December 1
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time at an accredited college, university, or technical institute following graduation

name: Texas Garden Clubs Scholarship
description: Annual scholarships for Texas resident students at the college junior level or above who are majoring in a horticulture-related field. Qualifying majors include floriculture, landscape design, horticulture, botany, biology, plant pathology, forestry, agronomy, environmental studies, and land management. The 2025 recipients received $4,000 and $3,000; the application deadline is October 1 for an award in the following spring/winter semester.

requirements.application: Mailed application to the Texas Garden Clubs VP of Scholarships

name: Texas Mutual Scholarship Program
description: Provides up to $6,600 for tuition, fees, books, and supplies to injured Texas workers and their dependents. Eligible applicants are workers with injuries qualifying for lifetime benefits under the Texas Workers' Compensation Act, plus unmarried children ages 16 to 25 and unmarried surviving spouses of workers killed or permanently injured while working for a Texas Mutual policyholder. Applications are due June 30 for the fall semester and October 31 for the spring semester.

eligibility.enrollment: Full-time
eligibility.special_circumstances: Injured worker qualifying for lifetime benefits under Texas Workers' Compensation Act Section 408.161, or an unmarried child or surviving spouse of such a worker employed by a Texas Mutual policyholder

name: Texas Farm Bureau Memorial/Honorary and District Scholarship
description: In each of Texas Farm Bureau's 13 districts, one graduating high school senior receives a $5,000 scholarship and three additional students receive $3,000 each. Applicants must be from a Texas Farm Bureau member family. The prior cycle closed March 2; the next cycle's deadline has not yet been posted but has historically fallen in early March.

requirements.application: Online application through Texas Farm Bureau

name: Texas Farm Bureau Young Farmer & Rancher Scholarship for High School Students
description: Each of Texas Farm Bureau's 13 districts awards one $1,500 scholarship to a graduating high school senior pursuing a degree in agriculture. Applicants must come from a Texas Farm Bureau member family. The prior cycle closed March 2; the next cycle's deadline has not yet been posted but has historically fallen in early March.

requirements.application: Online application through Texas Farm Bureau

name: Texas Farm Bureau Dick Mitchell Memorial Scholarship
description: A $1,000 scholarship awarded to one Texas high school senior who completed the Thrive Event through Texas Farm Bureau's Student Success Series. Only students who participated in the qualifying Thrive Event are eligible. The prior cycle closed March 2; the next cycle's deadline has not yet been posted.

eligibility.activity_requirement: Completed the Thrive Event through Texas Farm Bureau's Student Success Series

requirements.application: Online application through Texas Farm Bureau

name: Texas Elks State Association Four-Year Scholarship
description: A renewable award of up to $1,250 for Texas high school seniors who are not in the top 5 percent of their class and plan to pursue a bachelor's degree at an accredited Texas college or university. Students may begin at a junior college and transfer. Selection weighs scholarship, financial need, leadership and extracurricular activities, and character; males and females compete separately. The deadline has historically fallen in late February.

eligibility.residency: Texas resident attending a Texas high school
eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.class_rank: Not in the top 5 percent of class
eligibility.college_location: Accredited college or university in Texas
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time toward a bachelor's degree

requirements.application: Separate TESA application submitted through Texas Elks State Association

name: Texas DPS Scholarship
description: Awards of up to $5,000 for current or retired employees of the Texas Department of Public Safety and their immediate family members. Administered through the Communities Foundation of Texas universal scholarship application. The prior cycle closed May 15; the next cycle's date has not been posted, but CFT deadlines typically fall between March and May.

eligibility.affiliation: Current or retired Texas Department of Public Safety employee, or immediate family member

name: LIFE Association Trade Scholarship
description: Awards of up to $5,000 for graduating Texas high school seniors and past graduates pursuing a trade or vocational degree. One of the few Texas awards specifically targeted at skilled trades rather than four-year degrees. The prior cycle closed May 1; the next cycle's date has not been posted, but CFT deadlines typically fall between March and May.

name: Tri-County Electric Cooperative Scholarship
description: Forty $5,000 scholarships for high school seniors graduating in 2027 who live with a parent or legal guardian who is an active member of Tri-County Electric Cooperative, which serves 16 counties in north Texas from its Azle headquarters. Funds may be used at an accredited university, college, junior college, or technical school. Applications are accepted September 14, 2026 through January 15, 2027, with winners announced in April 2027.
