eligibility.notes: Must be 15-18 years old and in grades 10-12 as of December 1, 2026. Prior National YoungArts Week attendees are not eligible for the with-distinction award.

requirements.notes: Discipline-specific artistic submission (recordings, portfolio, or manuscript) reviewed by a blind panel.

name: Doodle for Google
description: A national art contest in which K-12 students redesign the Google logo around an annual theme. The national winner receives a $55,000 college scholarship plus a $50,000 technology package for their school; the 2026 theme was 'My superpower is...' and the winner was announced in June 2026. Dates for the next contest have not been posted yet; entries have historically been accepted in the winter and judged in the spring.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. residents
eligibility.notes: Open to K-12 students in the United States. Only the national winner's scholarship amount is confirmed by Google; state and national finalist prizes are announced with each year's rules.

requirements.notes: Original artwork plus a short written statement about the doodle's inspiration; parent or guardian signature required for minors.

name: Glenn Miller Birthplace Society Music Scholarship Competition
description: An annual vocal and instrumental music competition held during the Glenn Miller Festival in Clarinda, Iowa, honoring the bandleader's legacy. Ten vocal and ten instrumental semi-finalists are invited to compete in person, with first place winning $10,000, second $5,000, and third $3,000 in each category ($36,000 in total awards). The 2026 application closed April 20, 2026; the 2027 competition dates have not been posted yet.

eligibility.notes: Open to high school seniors and college freshmen nationwide who intend to make music their future focus. Two categories: vocal and instrumental.

requirements.notes: Recorded preliminary submission; semi-finalists must travel to Clarinda, Iowa to perform live during the festival in June.

name: Dr. Kenny D. Hasija Scholarship
description: A Thespian scholarship honoring Broadway producer Ken Davenport's father, supporting applicants who are traditionally underrepresented in the theatre industry. One award of $1,000 is given each year. Applications are accepted February 1 through April 1 and winners are announced in May.

eligibility.notes: Graduating high school seniors who are inducted Thespians; supports applicants traditionally underrepresented in theatre.

requirements.notes: Application through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal, which opens February 1.

name: Mark Drum Scholarship
description: Created with donations from Thespian alumni to support Asian and Pacific Islander Thespians pursuing theatre. One award of $1,250 is given annually. The application window runs February 1 through April 1, with winners announced in May.

eligibility.notes: Open to high school seniors and undergraduate college students who are Asian or Pacific Islander Thespians.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal.

name: Alan D. and Penny Lu Engelsman Scholarship
description: A Thespian scholarship for graduating high school seniors who plan to major in theatre or a related field. One award of $1,000 is given each year. Applications are accepted February 1 through April 1 and winners are announced in May.

eligibility.notes: High school seniors pursuing a theatre or theatre-related major.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal.

name: Future Theatre Educator Scholarship
description: Supports Thespians who intend to build a career teaching theatre. One award of $1,500 is given annually to a graduating senior enrolling as a theatre education major. Applications open February 1 and close April 1, with winners announced in May.

eligibility.notes: High school seniors enrolling as theatre education majors.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal.

name: Gai Laing Jones Theatre Education Scholarship
description: Awards up to $2,000 each to two college students pursuing a theatre education degree. Unlike most Thespian scholarships, this one is aimed at students already in college rather than graduating seniors. The application window is February 1 through April 1, with winners announced in May.

eligibility.notes: College juniors, seniors, or graduate students pursuing a theatre education degree. Award is 'up to $2,000'; two are given annually.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal.

name: Michael J. Peitz Leadership Scholarship
description: A $1,500 award for a graduating Thespian who has demonstrated strong leadership in their troupe, school, or community. One scholarship is given each year. Applications are accepted February 1 through April 1 with winners announced in May.

eligibility.notes: High school seniors demonstrating leadership ability.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal.

name: Christopher L. Hunt Scholarship
description: A $1,000 Thespian scholarship for a graduating senior who plans to study business or marketing, recognizing that the theatre industry needs strong business talent as well as performers. One award is given annually. The application window runs February 1 through April 1.

eligibility.notes: High school seniors pursuing a business or marketing degree.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the Educational Theatre Foundation scholarship portal.

name: mikeroweWORKS Work Ethic Scholarship
description: Mike Rowe's foundation funds training for people entering the skilled trades, from welding and HVAC to diesel tech, cosmetology, and culinary arts. In the first of four 2026 rounds the foundation awarded 322 scholarships totaling $3 million, with individual awards ranging from $500 to $34,000 and averaging $9,100. The final deadline of the year is October 31, 2026; earlier rounds closed April 30, June 30, and August 30.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.notes: Must enroll in an approved accredited program of two years or less. Four-year degree programs do not qualify.

requirements.notes: Applicants must sign the S.W.E.A.T. Pledge and answer four short questions about it, record a short introduction video, provide two references, and upload a transcript plus an official tuition bill.

name: Horatio Alger National Career & Technical Scholarship
description: Three hundred scholarships of $2,500 each for students entering community college or trade and vocational school in a program that leads directly to employment. Applicants must show household income of $100,000 or less and be under 35, and pre-requisite coursework does not qualify. The 2026 application has closed; the association says 2027 application information is coming.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.enrollment: Associate's degree, certificate, or diploma program at a not-for-profit community college or trade/vocational school, enrolled by September
eligibility.notes: Must have completed high school or equivalency by July 1. Students enrolled only in pre-requisite courses are not eligible.

requirements.notes: Applicants first complete an eligibility quiz; those who qualify receive the application link.

name: Horatio Alger John Rollins Career & Technical Scholarship
description: Eight $2,500 scholarships for Delaware residents attending a not-for-profit community college or trade/vocational school in Delaware. Same core criteria as the national CTE award: household income of $100,000 or less, under age 35, U.S. citizen, and enrollment in an employment-focused associate, certificate, or diploma program. The 2026 application has closed and 2027 details are pending.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen and Delaware resident
eligibility.enrollment: Associate's degree, certificate, or diploma program at a Delaware not-for-profit community college or trade/vocational school
eligibility.notes: Must have completed high school or equivalency by July 1 and enroll by September.

requirements.notes: Eligibility quiz first, then an application link for qualifying students.

name: Horatio Alger Valencia College Career & Technical Scholarship
description: Sixteen $2,500 scholarships reserved for students attending Valencia College in Orlando, Florida in an associate, certificate, or diploma program that leads to employment. Applicants must be U.S. citizens under 35 with household income of $100,000 or less. The 2026 cycle has closed and 2027 information has not been posted.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.enrollment: Valencia College, Orlando FL, in an associate's degree, certificate, or diploma program
eligibility.notes: Must have completed high school or equivalency by July 1 and enroll by September; pre-requisite coursework does not qualify.

requirements.notes: Eligibility quiz first, then an application link for qualifying students.

name: Horatio Alger Warren Webster Technical Scholarship
description: Four $2,500 scholarships for students attending Apollo Career Center, Edison State Community College, Hobart Institute of Welding, Rhodes State College, or the University of Northwestern Ohio. Eligible fields include construction trades, manufacturing and welding, engineering, graphic design, business administration, and sales or marketing. The 2026 application has closed and 2027 details are pending.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.enrollment: Apollo Career Center, Edison State Community College, Hobart Institute of Welding, Rhodes State College, or University of Northwestern Ohio
eligibility.notes: Must have completed high school or equivalency by July 1 and enroll by September.

requirements.notes: Eligibility quiz first, then an application link for qualifying students.

name: Horatio Alger John Hardin Hudiburg Career & Technical Scholarship
description: One $4,000 scholarship for a high school senior in the Grapevine-Colleyville, Hurst-Euless-Bedford, Keller, or Birdville Independent school districts in Texas who plans to attend a community college or trade/vocational school. Household income must be $100,000 or less. The 2026 application has closed; 2027 information is pending.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. citizen
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time high school senior in Grapevine-Colleyville, Hurst-Euless-Bedford, Keller, or Birdville ISD planning to attend a not-for-profit community college or trade/vocational school
eligibility.notes: Must enroll in an associate's degree, certificate, or diploma program by September.

requirements.notes: Eligibility quiz first, then an application link for qualifying students.

name: AWS Foundation National Scholarships
description: More than 130 donor-funded scholarships totaling over $700,000 for students pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree in welding or a related discipline. Individual awards range from $2,500 to more than $10,000 and funds are paid directly to the school for tuition, fees, books, and required equipment. Applications open December 1 and close March 1 for the following fall term; one application matches students to every award they qualify for.

eligibility.enrollment: Bachelor's or associate degree program in welding or a related discipline
eligibility.membership: Some awards prefer or require AWS student membership
eligibility.notes: Some national scholarships require demonstrated financial need, verified through the FAFSA Submission Summary and cost-of-attendance documentation.

requirements.notes: Personal statement on background, welding experience, and career goals; official transcript sent directly by the school; headshot photo; FAFSA documentation for need-based awards.

name: NTHS Jon H. Poteat Scholarship
description: The flagship NTHS scholarship, awarding 275 scholarships of $1,000 each to active National Technical Honor Society members in career and technical education programs. Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal. The window runs September 1 through May 1 each year.

eligibility.membership: Active National Technical Honor Society member
eligibility.notes: Open to active NTHS members in career and technical education programs; 275 awards given annually.

requirements.notes: Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal.

name: NTHS Build Your Future Scholarship
description: Five $2,000 scholarships for high school seniors and post-secondary students studying construction-related disciplines. Applications run October 1 through April 1 through the NTHS Member Portal.

eligibility.membership: Active National Technical Honor Society member
eligibility.notes: For students in construction-related disciplines; 5 awards given annually.

requirements.notes: Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal.

name: NTHS C. Allen Powell Alumni Scholarship
description: Five $1,000 scholarships reserved for NTHS alumni, who gain lifetime access to this award beginning six months after graduation. This is a useful option for adults returning to school for additional trade credentials. The application window runs September 1 through May 1.

eligibility.notes: Available to NTHS alumni starting six months after graduation, with lifetime eligibility; 5 awards given annually.

requirements.notes: Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal.

name: NTHS SkillsUSA Partnership Scholarship
description: Four $1,000 scholarships for students who hold dual membership in both the National Technical Honor Society and SkillsUSA. The application window runs January 6 through April 15 each year.

eligibility.membership: Dual membership in NTHS and SkillsUSA required
eligibility.notes: 4 awards given annually.

requirements.notes: Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal; proof of dual membership required.

name: NTHS TechForce Partnership Scholarship
description: Two $2,500 scholarships for students with dual membership in the National Technical Honor Society and TechForce, aimed at students training as transportation and vehicle technicians. The deadline is May 31.

eligibility.membership: Dual membership in NTHS and TechForce required
eligibility.notes: 2 awards given annually.

requirements.notes: Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal; proof of dual membership required.

name: NTHS FFA Partnership Scholarship
description: Three $1,000 scholarships for students who hold dual membership in the National Technical Honor Society and the National FFA Organization. The application window runs November 1 through January 15.

eligibility.membership: Dual membership in NTHS and FFA required
eligibility.notes: 3 awards given annually.

requirements.notes: Applications are submitted through the NTHS Member Portal; proof of dual membership required.

name: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
description: More than 60 distinct scholarships for students pursuing associate or bachelor's degrees in manufacturing, engineering, and related technical fields, all reachable through a single application. Awards range from $2,500 to $20,000 and include both one-time and renewing scholarships, merit-based and need-based. Applications are accepted annually from November 1 to February 1.

eligibility.enrollment: Associate or bachelor's degree program in a technical field that directly supports manufacturing
eligibility.notes: Open to graduating high school seniors and current college students. One application is considered for every scholarship the student qualifies for.

requirements.notes: Register and create an account on the SME Education Foundation portal; some awards are need-based and some are merit-based.

name: SkillsUSA Make Your Mark Scholarship
description: A partnership scholarship providing SkillsUSA members up to $5,000 toward tuition, books, tools, on-campus housing, and other approved educational expenses. More than 450 scholarships have been awarded since the program launched in 2023. Deadlines are set per academic term and are announced on the SkillsUSA scholarships page rather than on a fixed annual date.

eligibility.notes: Awards are 'up to $5,000'; actual amounts vary by applicant and term of enrollment.

requirements.notes: Applications are posted on the SkillsUSA scholarships and grants page for each term; contact customercare@skillsusa.org for the current cycle.

name: Chick Evans Caddie Scholarship
provider_name: Western Golf Association / Evans Scholars Foundation
description: A full tuition and housing scholarship for golf caddies with strong academic records and demonstrated financial need, renewable for four years at a partner university. Applicants must have a strong caddie record, have finished junior year with above a B average in college-prep courses, and show outstanding character and leadership. Applications for the 2027-28 academic year became available August 1, 2026; the application and supporting evaluations should be complete by September 30, with the CSS Profile due October 15. Note: the Western Golf Association does not publish a fixed dollar value for this award, so the amount range shown is an approximate annual value of tuition and housing rather than a stated award amount.

eligibility.notes: Must have a strong caddie record at a sponsoring club, above a B average in college-prep courses through junior year, and demonstrated financial need. Award is full tuition and housing at a partner university; the dollar range shown is an approximate annual value of tuition and housing, not a fixed cash award.

requirements.notes: High School Evaluation, Caddie Evaluation, transcript, and test scores due September 30; CSS Profile submitted to College Board by October 15.

name: USBC Alberta E. Crowe Star of Tomorrow Award
description: A $6,000 scholarship recognizing star qualities in a female high school junior or senior who competes in bowling, judged on certified bowling performance at local through national levels, academic achievement, and civic involvement. Winners may only receive this award once. The 2027 application window has not been posted; the award is presented each spring at the USBC Annual Meeting.

eligibility.notes: Female bowlers age 21 or under who are high school juniors or seniors. One-time award.

requirements.notes: Application documents bowling performance at local, regional, state, and national levels along with academics and community involvement.

name: USBC Chuck Hall Star of Tomorrow Award
description: A $6,000 scholarship for a male high school junior or senior who competes in bowling, scored on distinguished certified bowling performance, academic achievement, and extracurricular and civic involvement. Like its counterpart award, it may be won only once. Application dates for the next cycle have not been posted.

eligibility.notes: Male bowlers who are high school juniors or seniors. One-time award.

requirements.notes: Application documents bowling performance at local, regional, state, and national levels along with academics and community involvement.

name: USBC Earl Anthony Memorial Scholarship
description: Five $5,000 scholarships for high school juniors and seniors with strong community involvement, academic achievement, and demonstrated financial need. Notably, bowling performance is not a judging factor, so this is accessible to any USBC youth member regardless of average. Application dates for the next cycle have not been posted.

eligibility.notes: Bowling performance is not considered. Financial need is required. Five awards; one-time only.

requirements.notes: Application covers community involvement, academics, and financial need.

name: USBC Annual Zeb Scholarship
description: A $2,500 scholarship for a high school junior or senior who is a USBC member in good standing, awarded primarily on community service and academic success. It is a one-time award. Application dates for the next cycle have not been posted.

eligibility.membership: Current USBC member in good standing
eligibility.notes: Selection is based primarily on community service and academic success.

requirements.notes: Application documents community service and academic record.

name: USBC Gift for Life Scholarship
description: Up to twelve $1,000 scholarships each year for USBC high school members with at least a 2.0 GPA who can demonstrate financial need. Two awards are reserved annually for children of fire, rescue, and police personnel. Application dates for the next cycle have not been posted.

eligibility.notes: Financial need required. Two of the twelve awards are reserved for children of fire, rescue, or police personnel.

requirements.notes: Application documents GPA and financial need.

name: USBC Youth Ambassador of the Year
description: One male and one female USBC youth member are each named Youth Ambassador of the Year and receive a $1,500 scholarship for their contributions to bowling, academics, and community involvement. Selected ambassadors may also serve on the Youth Advisory Group for additional funds. Applicants must be at least 18 by August 1; application dates for the next cycle have not been posted.

eligibility.notes: High school juniors or seniors who will be at least 18 by August 1. One male and one female selected.

requirements.notes: Application documents contributions to the sport, academics, and community involvement.

name: Dexter High School All-American Team
provider_name: United States Bowling Congress and Dexter
description: Ten high school bowlers, five male and five female, are named to the Dexter High School All-American Team and receive $1,000 each, with an additional $500 for the team captain. Applicants need a 3.0 GPA, membership on a high school varsity or club team, a coach or athletic director recommendation, and an essay. Applications for the current cycle are closed; dates for the next cycle have not been posted.

eligibility.notes: Must be a member of a high school varsity or club bowling team. Ten athletes selected: five male, five female.

requirements.notes: Requires a recommendation from a coach or athletic director.

name: ARRL Foundation Scholarships
description: The ARRL Foundation administers more than 170 donor-established scholarships for licensed amateur radio operators, ranging from $500 to $25,000, all reachable through a single online application. Every applicant must hold an active FCC amateur radio license; some individual awards add requirements such as a letter from an officer of an ARRL-affiliated club. The 2026 cycle ran October 30 to December 30, 2025 and recipients were notified in June, so the next cycle is expected to open in the fall.

eligibility.notes: Some awards have additional geographic, school, or field-of-study restrictions. Active foreign amateur radio operators are eligible for the ADRC scholarships.

requirements.notes: Transcripts and supporting documents must be uploaded with the application rather than emailed separately. Some scholarships require a recommendation letter from a sitting officer of an ARRL-affiliated club.

name: The Vegetarian Resource Group Scholarship
description: Awards one $10,000 scholarship and five $5,000 scholarships to graduating U.S. high school seniors who have actively promoted veganism in their schools or communities. Judges look for compassion, courage, and commitment rather than grades alone, and applicants document their advocacy with photos, news coverage, and similar evidence. Early submissions are accepted starting December 1, 2026, and the deadline is February 20, 2027.

eligibility.citizenship: U.S. residents; payment is made only to U.S.-based colleges
eligibility.notes: Must be graduating from high school in spring 2027.

requirements.notes: Essay addressing 16 topics on vegan advocacy, transcripts or report cards for the past two years, three or more recommendation letters including at least one from a teacher, plus documentation of advocacy work.

name: NESA Lawrence S. and Mabel Cooke Scholarship
description: The largest NESA award: one four-year scholarship of $50,000 ($12,500 per year) and four four-year scholarships of $30,000 ($7,500 per year) for Eagle Scouts who are NESA members. Applicants may apply from their senior year of high school through their junior year of an undergraduate program, must enroll full time, and cannot attend a U.S. military academy. For the 2026 cycle the portal opened December 1 and closed January 31; the next cycle is expected on a similar schedule.

eligibility.membership: Eagle Scout rank and NESA membership required
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time undergraduate enrollment, minimum 12 credit hours
eligibility.notes: Eligible from senior year of high school through junior year of an undergraduate program. Not available to graduate students or students attending U.S. military academies. Only one NESA scholarship may be awarded per recipient.

requirements.notes: Eagle Board of Review must be completed by the date published for each cycle (on or before January 24 for the 2026 cycle).

name: NESA One-Year Eagle Scout Scholarships
description: A family of one-year awards for Eagle Scouts who are NESA members, including the Cooke one-year scholarship at $10,000, the Hansen & Mary Hall award at $7,000, the NESA Scholarship Endowment and Legacy Society awards at $6,000 each, and the Tappan Scholarship at $5,000. Most are awarded once per Central Service Territory, so 14 of each are given nationally. The 2026 portal ran December 1 to January 31 and awards were announced June 10; the next cycle is expected on a similar schedule.

eligibility.membership: Eagle Scout rank and NESA membership required
eligibility.enrollment: Full-time undergraduate enrollment, minimum 12 credit hours
eligibility.notes: Eligible from senior year of high school through junior year of an undergraduate program, or the halfway point of an associate or trade program. Only one NESA scholarship per recipient.

requirements.notes: A single NESA application is considered for the full family of awards.

name: Chick and Sophie Major Memorial Duck Calling Contest
description: A duck calling competition for students held on the Main Street stage in Stuttgart, Arkansas alongside the World's Champion Duck Calling Contest during the Wings Over the Prairie Festival, typically the weekend after Thanksgiving. The contest awards $9,000 in scholarships: $5,000 for first place, $2,000 for second, $1,250 for third, and $750 for fourth. Contestants must appear in person and register with photo ID and proof of age; the date and registration deadline for the next contest have not been posted.

eligibility.notes: Open to any current student ages 16-20 furthering their education through traditional school, trade school, or other educational and career pathways. Seniors must perform a Main Street duck calling routine for eligibility.

requirements.notes: In-person performance in Stuttgart, Arkansas. Photo ID and proof of age required at registration.

name: Duck Brand Stuck at Prom Scholarship Contest
description: Students design and wear prom attire made from Duck Tape and submit photos for judging plus a public vote. Two first prize winners, one in the dress category and one in the tux category, each receive a $10,000 scholarship, and eight runners-up receive $1,000 each plus a prize pack. The 2026 contest ran March 25 to July 13 with entries due June 3; the 2027 contest has not been announced but has opened in late March in recent years.

eligibility.citizenship: Legal residents of the U.S., D.C., Puerto Rico, and U.S. territories (excluding Maryland, Colorado, Nebraska, and North Dakota) or Canada (excluding Quebec)
eligibility.enrollment: Enrolled in a high school or home school association at the high school level
eligibility.notes: Prior contest finalists are not eligible. Attending prom is not required.

requirements.notes: One to five high-resolution color photos of the entrant wearing the attire, plus written or video detail about the outfit. Paid professionals may not assist; friends and family may. Parent or guardian consent required for minors.

name: Niche $2,000 No Essay Scholarship
description: A recurring-drawing scholarship from the college search site Niche: one student receives $2,000 toward tuition, housing, books, or other college costs with no essay required. The winner is chosen by random drawing and contacted by Votigo, Niche's scholarship fulfillment partner, and only one entry per person is allowed per cycle. The current cycle closes August 31, 2026, and Niche opens a new no-essay drawing on a rolling basis.

eligibility.citizenship: Legal U.S. residents
eligibility.notes: Open to high school students, college students, or anyone planning to enroll in college within the next 12 months. No minimum GPA.

requirements.notes: Registration form only. This is a recurring-drawing sweepstakes-style award, not a merit competition: the winner is selected at random. One entry per person.

name: NRF Foundation Next Generation Scholarship
description: The highest student honor from the National Retail Federation Foundation, with a top award of $25,000 and recognition as an emerging leader in retail. Finalists are named publicly and attend the NRF Foundation Student Program in New York City, held January 7-10, 2027. Application dates for the current cycle have not been posted on the scholarships page.

eligibility.notes: Undergraduate students with an interest in retail careers. The $25,000 figure is the top award; smaller finalist awards are also given.

requirements.notes: Application includes essays about retail career interest and leadership; finalists are interviewed.

name: NRF Foundation University Challenge Scholarship
description: A business case competition for teams of three to four undergraduates from any major, in which teams pitch to retail leaders and can earn up to $30,000 in scholarships. The 2026-27 University Challenge is announced as opening soon on the NRF Foundation scholarships page. Registration dates have not yet been posted.

eligibility.notes: Teams of three to four undergraduate students studying any major. The $30,000 figure is the maximum a team can earn, split among members.

requirements.notes: Team case study submission followed by a live pitch to retail executives.

name: Beinecke Scholarship
description: Awards $35,000 total, disbursed over up to five years, to college juniors planning research or creative-focused master's or doctoral study in the arts, humanities, or social sciences. Applicants must have a documented history of eligibility for need-based financial aid as undergraduates. Only students at the roughly 120 participating institutions may be nominated, and each campus submits through a designated liaison; the 2026 nomination deadline was March 27, 2026, and the cycle typically closes in late March.

eligibility.notes: Must attend a participating institution and plan to enter a research or creative-focused graduate program.

name: Gilman Critical Need Language Award
provider_name: U.S. Department of State / Institute of International Education
description: A supplemental award of up to $3,000 layered on top of the base Gilman Scholarship for students who study a language designated as critical to U.S. national security while abroad. It is requested inside the standard Gilman application, so there is no separate form or deadline. Recipients commit to continuing language study and to a follow-on service project.

eligibility.notes: Must be a Gilman applicant studying a designated critical need language abroad.

requirements.notes: Applied for within the standard Gilman Scholarship application.

name: Boren Scholarship
description: Funds U.S. undergraduates to study less commonly taught languages in world regions critical to U.S. interests, including Africa, Asia, Eurasia, Latin America, and the Middle East. Awards are tied to duration abroad: $25,000 for 25 to 52 weeks (the preferred length), $12,500 for 12 to 24 weeks, and $8,000 for 8 to 11 weeks for STEM majors only. Recipients take on a one-year federal service requirement in a national security-related position after graduation.

eligibility.notes: Study must be outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. Award size depends on program duration.

name: Freeman-ASIA Award
provider_name: Institute of International Education / Freeman Foundation
description: Need-based study abroad funding for U.S. undergraduates studying in East or Southeast Asia, worth up to $3,000 for summer, $5,000 for a semester or quarter, and $7,000 for an academic or calendar year. Students at both two-year and four-year institutions are eligible. Applications require certification from both the study abroad adviser and the financial aid adviser; the 2026-2027 cycle closed April 7, 2026, and the next cycle is expected to open in February 2027.

eligibility.enrollment_status: undergraduate at a two-year or four-year U.S. institution

name: Fund for Education Abroad Scholarships
description: A portfolio of study abroad scholarships for U.S. undergraduates with financial need, with individual awards running from $1,000 to $10,000 depending on the named fund and program length. FEA awarded $360,750 across 108 undergraduates for its most recent Summer/Fall 2026 and Academic Year 2026-27 cohort. Applicants must not have previously studied abroad since high school; the Summer/Fall application typically opens November to early February and the Winter/Spring application late July to mid-September.

eligibility.notes: Must not have previously studied abroad after high school graduation. Program must be at least 14 days and credit-bearing. Graduate students are not eligible.

requirements.notes: Financial need shown via Student Aid Index below 20,000, Pell eligibility, or current student loan debt.

name: Phi Kappa Phi Study Abroad Grant
provider_name: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi
description: Fifty grants of $1,000 each go to undergraduates studying abroad, and Phi Kappa Phi membership is not required as long as your institution has an active chapter. Applicants need a cumulative GPA of 3.75 or higher with no rounding, and the study abroad program must begin between May 1, 2027 and June 30, 2028. Each student may receive the grant only once.

eligibility.enrollment_status: undergraduate at an institution with an active Phi Kappa Phi chapter
eligibility.notes: Program must begin between May 1, 2027 and June 30, 2028. One-time award.

name: Phi Kappa Phi Fellowship
provider_name: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi
description: For graduating seniors and recent Phi Kappa Phi members entering their first year of graduate or professional school: 40 fellowships of $8,500, six of $15,000, and two of $35,000. Applicants must be active members with dues paid through the deadline and must begin graduate study between May 1, 2027 and February 1, 2028, having completed no more than nine graduate credits. Chapters set internal deadlines roughly two weeks before the national date.

eligibility.notes: Must be an active Phi Kappa Phi member with dues paid through April 15, 2027, entering full-time graduate or professional study between May 1, 2027 and February 1, 2028, with no more than 9 graduate credits completed.

name: Jack Kent Cooke Foundation Undergraduate Transfer Scholarship
description: The largest private scholarship in the country for community college transfer students, providing last-dollar funding of as much as $55,000 per year for two to three years to finish a bachelor's degree. Roughly 65 awards are made annually from thousands of applications. Applicants must be sophomores at a U.S. community or two-year college by January 1, 2027 (or graduates since spring 2022), carry a 3.5 or higher cumulative GPA, plan full-time bachelor's enrollment in fall 2027, and generally must not have previously attended a four-year institution.

eligibility.notes: Must be enrolled at a U.S. community college or two-year institution with sophomore status by January 1, 2027, or a graduate since spring 2022. Cannot have previously attended a four-year college, with limited exceptions for dual enrollment.

name: Hites Transfer Scholarship
description: Awards up to $7,500 to Phi Theta Kappa members transferring from a two-year college to a four-year institution, recognizing academic rigor, campus and community engagement, and leadership. Applicants must be enrolled in six or more semester credits of associate-level coursework through December, have completed at least 45 semester credits by December, and hold a 3.5 or higher GPA on coursework from the last five years.

eligibility.notes: Must be a PTK member in good standing planning full-time transfer to an accredited four-year institution, with an academic record free from suspension or probation.

requirements.notes: Submitted through the single PTK common scholarship application.

name: Guistwhite Scholarship
description: Awards up to $5,000 to Phi Theta Kappa members transferring to a four-year institution, weighted toward chapter participation and society programs alongside leadership and academics. Requirements mirror the Hites award: six or more current semester credits, 45 or more completed by December, a 3.5 minimum GPA on the last five years of coursework, and plans to enroll full time at a regionally accredited four-year college.

eligibility.notes: Emphasizes engagement in PTK chapter activities and societal programs.

name: Coca-Cola Leaders of Promise Scholarship
provider_name: Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society / Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation
description: Awards up to $1,000 to Phi Theta Kappa members early in their community college careers, helping them complete an associate degree and stay engaged in chapter leadership. Applicants must be enrolled in six or more semester credits and have completed between 12 and 36 semester credits by January 31 of the application year, with a 3.5 or higher GPA and no prior associate or bachelor's degree.

eligibility.notes: Must continue in a two-year associate degree program the following fall and hold residency status eligible for federal financial aid.

name: Coca-Cola Military Leaders of Promise Scholarship
provider_name: Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society / Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation
description: Awards up to $1,000 to Phi Theta Kappa members who are military members, veterans, or their spouses or dependents. Eligibility otherwise tracks the standard Leaders of Promise award: six or more current semester credits, 12 to 36 credits completed by the deadline, a 3.5 or higher GPA, and no associate or bachelor's degree already earned.

eligibility.notes: Open to military members, veterans, and their spouses or dependents.

name: All-USA Academic Team Scholarship
provider_name: Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society / American Association of Community Colleges
description: Twenty community college students are named to the All-USA Academic Team each year and receive a $5,000 scholarship, selected for intellectual rigor, academic achievement, leadership, and civic growth from a pool of more than 2,000 nominees. Students must be nominated by their college, be enrolled in six or more semester credits through December, have completed 36 or more credits by December, and hold a 3.5 or higher GPA on coursework from the last five years.

eligibility.notes: Must be nominated by your community college. No prior All-USA or Coca-Cola Academic Team nomination.

name: New Century Transfer Pathway Scholarship
provider_name: Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society / Coca-Cola Foundation / AACC
description: Awards up to $2,750 to one high-achieving transfer-bound community college student per state, sponsored by The Coca-Cola Foundation, the Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation, the American Association of Community Colleges, and Phi Theta Kappa. Applicants must be nominated by their college for the All-USA Academic Team, be enrolled in six or more semester credits through December, have completed 36 or more credits by December, and hold a 3.5 or higher GPA.

eligibility.notes: Must plan to enroll at a four-year college the following fall and be nominated for the All-USA Academic Team.

name: New Century Workforce Pathway Scholarship
provider_name: Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society / Coca-Cola Foundation / AACC
description: Awards up to $1,500 to community college students who plan to enter the workforce directly after finishing a two-year credential rather than transferring. Applicants must be nominated by their college for the All-USA Academic Team, be enrolled in at least six semester credits through December, have completed 12 or more credits by December, and hold a 3.5 or higher GPA on coursework from the last five years.

eligibility.notes: For students planning to enter the workforce after completing a two-year college credential.

name: American Medical Student Association Scholarship (Phi Theta Kappa)
provider_name: Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society / American Medical Student Association
description: Awards up to $5,000 to Phi Theta Kappa members in pre-med or related programs at two-year institutions who plan to transfer to a four-year college and ultimately attend medical school. Applicants need at least six current semester credits, 45 or more credits completed by December 31, and a 3.5 or higher GPA on coursework from the last five years.

eligibility.notes: Must plan full-time transfer to a four-year regionally accredited college and intend to pursue medical school.

name: Christopher Calhoun Transfer Scholarship
description: Awards up to $1,000 to a Phi Theta Kappa member enrolled at a South Carolina two-year institution who plans to transfer to a four-year accredited college the following fall. Applicants must be U.S. citizens nominated by their college for the All-USA Academic Team and must meet the associated All-USA criteria.

eligibility.notes: Must be enrolled at a South Carolina two-year institution.

name: Jo Anne J. Trow Undergraduate Scholarship
provider_name: Alpha Lambda Delta National Honor Society
description: Alpha Lambda Delta distributes 50 undergraduate scholarships ranging from $2,000 to $6,000, totaling about $140,000 each year, to members continuing their studies. Applicants must have been inducted at least in the spring or fall of the year prior to the deadline, have at least one year remaining before graduation, and carry a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher. The selection committee begins review in mid-February with decisions announced in June, and a student may receive the award only once.

eligibility.notes: Must be enrolled at an institution with an active Alpha Lambda Delta chapter and have at least one year remaining before graduation.

name: Golden Key Undergraduate Achievement Award
description: A $1,000 award open exclusively to undergraduate Golden Key members worldwide, recognizing accomplishment across the undergraduate career. Golden Key invites students in the top 15 percent of their class, so membership comes first. The most recent listed deadline in the society's scholarship portal was June 15, 2026, and the cycle historically closes in mid-June.

eligibility.notes: Members only, undergraduates only. Golden Key membership is by invitation to students in the top 15 percent of their class.

name: Golden Key Outstanding Member Award
description: A $500 award for Golden Key members who have made a notable contribution to their chapter and society, open to undergraduates and available worldwide. It is administered through the same scholarship portal as the society's other awards, which most recently listed a June 15, 2026 deadline.

eligibility.notes: Open to Golden Key members; not restricted to undergraduates but undergraduates are eligible.

name: Tau Sigma National Scholarship
description: Tau Sigma is the national honor society specifically for transfer students, and its national chapter awards scholarships annually to members. The most recent cycle distributed $100,000 with individual awards from $500 to $5,000. Applications are submitted through your chapter advisor, who receives the announcement each fall; awards are announced in December and paid in late January, with applications generally due in mid-November.

eligibility.notes: Must be an active member of Tau Sigma, the national honor society for transfer students, at a campus with a chapter.

requirements.notes: Applications are distributed by and returned through your chapter advisor.

name: BHE Foundation Emerging Leaders Scholarship
description: Twenty NSCS members receive $10,000 each through this STEM-focused award, the society's largest scholarship program at $200,000 annually. Applicants must be NSCS members in good standing with a minimum 3.0 GPA, and selection weighs academics, leadership, and service. Applications run through the NSCS scholarship portal, which is updated throughout the year.

name: GEICO Changemaker Award
description: Six NSCS members receive $10,000 each across six categories in this Student of the Year program, recognizing members who have created measurable change on campus or in their communities. Membership in NSCS and a minimum 3.0 GPA are required, and selection is based on academics, leadership, and service.

name: NSCS College Impact Award
description: A $1,000 award for NSCS members who have had a meaningful impact on their college community; two were granted in 2025. NSCS distributes over $750,000 in scholarships annually and requires a minimum 3.0 GPA of undergraduate members. Applications are submitted through the NSCS scholarship portal.

name: NSCS Scholar at Sea Award
provider_name: National Society of Collegiate Scholars (NSCS) / Semester at Sea
description: A partner scholarship of $5,000 to $10,000 for NSCS members sailing with Semester at Sea, layered on top of Semester at Sea's own merit and need-based grants. Twelve were awarded in 2025. Applicants must be NSCS members in good standing and admitted to a Semester at Sea voyage.

eligibility.notes: Must be admitted to a Semester at Sea voyage.

name: Semester at Sea Need-Based Grant
provider_name: Institute for Shipboard Education (Semester at Sea)
description: Need-based grants from $250 to $10,000 toward a Semester at Sea voyage, open to all admitted students. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until roughly two weeks before the voyage departs or until funds are exhausted, so applying early materially improves your odds. Pell Grant recipients can additionally receive a Pell Grant Match.

eligibility.notes: Open to all admitted Semester at Sea students. Rolling review until about two weeks before the voyage or until funds run out.

name: Semester at Sea Merit Grant
provider_name: Institute for Shipboard Education (Semester at Sea)
description: Merit grants from $250 to $2,500 toward a Semester at Sea voyage for admitted students with a GPA above 3.0. Like the need-based grants, these are reviewed on a rolling basis until about two weeks before departure or until funds are depleted.

eligibility.notes: Rolling review until about two weeks before the voyage or until funds run out.

name: Semester at Sea Alumni Funded Scholarship
provider_name: Institute for Shipboard Education (Semester at Sea)
description: Alumni-funded scholarships of $500 to $10,000 for students sailing with Semester at Sea. The Spring 2027 voyage application opened July 7, 2026 and closes September 5, 2026; the Fall 2027 voyage application opens February 8, 2027 and closes April 23, 2027.

eligibility.notes: Must be admitted to a Semester at Sea voyage. Deadline shown is for the Spring 2027 voyage; the Fall 2027 deadline is April 23, 2027.

name: Semester at Sea Student Assistant Grant
provider_name: Institute for Shipboard Education (Semester at Sea)
description: A $4,000 grant for students who serve as shipboard assistants during a Semester at Sea voyage, combining a work role with study abroad funding. The Spring 2027 voyage application closes September 5, 2026, and the Fall 2027 application closes April 23, 2027.

eligibility.notes: Must be admitted to a Semester at Sea voyage and selected for a student assistant role.

name: Semester at Sea Inclusive Engagement Scholarship
provider_name: Institute for Shipboard Education (Semester at Sea)
description: A $5,000 scholarship plus covered flights for students sailing with Semester at Sea, awarded through the voyage scholarship application. The Spring 2027 voyage application opened July 7, 2026 and closes September 5, 2026; the Fall 2027 cycle closes April 23, 2027.

eligibility.notes: Must be admitted to a Semester at Sea voyage. Award includes flights in addition to the $5,000.

name: Scholarship America Dream Award
description: One of the few large national awards built specifically for students already in college: renewable awards of up to $10,000 per year for undergraduates who have completed at least one year of full-time study. Awards renew for up to three additional years or until a first bachelor's degree is earned. Applicants must be at least 17, hold a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA, be pursuing a first associate or bachelor's degree, and demonstrate financial need. The 2027 cycle has not opened; semi-finalists are typically notified in January.

eligibility.notes: Must have completed at least one year of full-time undergraduate study. High school seniors are excluded.

name: Jeannette Rankin National Scholar Grant
description: Unrestricted, non-tuition grants of up to $2,500 per year for women and nonbinary students aged 35 and older pursuing technical or vocational training, an associate degree, or a first bachelor's degree. Because the funds are unrestricted, they can cover childcare, transportation, and living costs that standard aid will not touch. Grants renew for up to five years, and the most recent cycle ran November 3, 2025 through February 13, 2026.

eligibility.notes: Must be pursuing technical or vocational education, an associate degree, or a first bachelor's degree at an accredited U.S. institution.

name: Patsy Takemoto Mink Education Support Award
description: Five awards of up to $5,000 each for low-income mothers pursuing post-secondary education, disbursed in two installments across the academic year and usable for direct school expenses or living expenses. Applicants must be women at least 17 years old with minor children, enrolled full time in a degree program more advanced than any they have already completed, at an accredited non-profit U.S. institution. The 2026-27 cycle closed August 1, 2026; details for 2027-28 are posted in May 2027.

eligibility.notes: Family income limits range from about $21,640 to $33,000 depending on family size. Must be pursuing a degree level more advanced than any previously completed.

name: Soroptimist Live Your Dream Award
description: Cash awards for women who are the primary financial provider for themselves and their dependents while pursuing vocational training or an undergraduate degree. Awards are made in tiers: about $1,000 at the club level, $3,000 to $5,000 at the region level, and $10,000 at the international level, so a single recipient can accumulate up to $16,000 as she advances. Funds may go toward tuition, books, transportation, and childcare. Applications are accepted August 1 through November 15.

eligibility.notes: Must reside in a Soroptimist International of the Americas member country, be enrolled in or accepted to vocational training or an undergraduate program, and not hold or be pursuing a graduate degree. Prior Women's Opportunity or Live Your Dream recipients are ineligible.

requirements.notes: Written sections must be in the applicant's own words; AI may assist only with grammar and organization.

name: P.E.O. Program for Continuing Education (PCE) Grant
description: A one-time need-based grant of up to $4,000 for women whose education was interrupted and who are returning to finish a degree or certification that will improve their employment prospects. Applicants must have spent at least 24 consecutive months out of formal education during adulthood and be within roughly 18 months of completing their program. There is no fixed annual deadline: a local P.E.O. chapter must first sponsor you, after which you receive an online application with a 30-day window.

eligibility.notes: Must be within 18 consecutive months of completing the program and must not already hold a master's degree or higher. Requires sponsorship by a local P.E.O. chapter.

requirements.notes: Cannot fund living expenses, loan repayment, or prerequisite courses.

name: Osher Reentry Scholarship
provider_name: Bernard Osher Foundation (administered by participating universities)
description: A national program for adults returning to finish a first bachelor's degree after a cumulative break of five or more years, typically aged 25 to 50. The Osher Foundation funds participating colleges and universities, and each campus sets its own amounts and deadlines: UC Berkeley, for example, awards up to $5,000 for the academic year. Students apply through their own institution, not the Foundation, so check the Foundation's list of participating schools and then contact your campus financial aid office.

eligibility.notes: Must be pursuing a first baccalaureate degree at a participating institution. Graduate students, students seeking additional degrees, online-only students, and international students planning to return home are excluded. Amounts and deadlines vary by campus; the range shown reflects UC Berkeley's published maximum.

name: Davis-Putter Scholarship Fund
description: Need-based grants of up to $15,000 per year for students who are active organizers in progressive movements for liberation, self-determination, and social and economic justice. The average grant for 2025-26 was $7,700. Open to students in degree, certificate, and trade or technical programs, with preference for those without access to family wealth and applicants from under-resourced and rural areas. Applications close at midnight EST on April 1, with decisions in July.

eligibility.enrollment_status: enrolled in a post-secondary degree, certificate, or trade/technical program

name: Charles B. Rangel International Affairs Summer Enrichment Program
provider_name: Charles B. Rangel International Affairs Program / U.S. Department of State
description: A fully funded six-week summer program in Washington, D.C. for undergraduates considering careers in international affairs and the Foreign Service. Participants receive a $3,300 stipend, and the program covers tuition, travel, housing, and two meals a day. Applicants must be full-time undergraduates with at least sophomore standing, U.S. citizenship, and a cumulative GPA of 3.2 or higher; applications close in early February with notifications in mid to late March.

eligibility.notes: Must have at least sophomore standing at the time of application.

name: Obama-Chesky Voyager Scholarship for Public Service
description: Selects students in their second year of undergraduate study who will start their third year in the fall, providing up to $25,000 per year in last-dollar financial aid for junior and senior years. Scholars also receive a $10,000 stipend plus free Airbnb housing for a summer work-travel experience between junior and senior year, and a $2,000 Airbnb travel credit annually for ten years after graduation. Applications for the current cohort are closed; watch the Foundation site for the next cycle.

eligibility.notes: Identifies students in their second year of undergraduate study who will be starting their third year in the fall. Aid is last-dollar, so amounts depend on remaining need.

name: Tillman Scholars Program
description: Supports active duty service members, veterans, and military spouses (including surviving spouses) pursuing bachelor's, master's, and professional degrees, with an average scholarship of $10,000 per academic year and amounts scaled to individual need and cost of attendance. About 60 scholars are selected annually from a highly competitive pool. Full-time enrollment at an accredited U.S. institution is required; there is no minimum GPA to apply, but scholars must maintain a 3.0 to renew. Applications typically open December 1.

eligibility.notes: Open to active duty service members across all branches, pre- and post-9/11 veterans, and military spouses or surviving spouses. Amount shown is the average award; individual amounts vary with need.

name: VFW Sport Clips Help A Hero Scholarship
provider_name: Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) / Sport Clips
description: Scholarships of up to $5,000 per semester for enlisted service members and veterans at rank E-5 or below who demonstrate financial need. Funds are restricted to tuition and fees and are paid directly to the school, and one award is allowed per family per semester. Fall applications run January 1 to April 30; spring applications run August 1 to November 15, with awards distributed in August and January respectively.

eligibility.notes: Must be retired, honorably discharged, active duty, National Guard, or Reserve, at rank E-5 or below, having completed basic and advanced individual training, and enrolled in or accepted to a VA-approved program at an accredited institution.
